chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Mercer Ellington and the Ellington band after Duke
summary: Mingus says the band should drop Ellington's book; Mercer and his father's coolness toward him.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. It's interesting, Mercer trying to keep that band together. It sounds less and less Ellington as the time goes on, and yet, how else could you be? But it's like -- it's not going to be an Ellington band very long.
Well, they shouldn't do what they're doing with Glenn Miller's music. Ellington's a great composer.
Yeah.
He should forget that bullshit and go out and get his own band together.
That's right. But I didn't know that Mercer was that good a writer.
He is that good.
That was sort of --
Mercer told me he was better than his father.
Really?
At one time in his life.
His father really did not encourage him as a musician.
Yeah, well, he cursed his father out and everything.
Yeah.

Fuck him, man, in Juillard they're doing that. I learned how to do that 20 years ago. He's not doing nothing. I got some things that upset him. I don't know if he meant it or if he wanted to see what I was saying. I just about (inaudible).
I just started this book on his father. And he starts out by saying there were times when he hated him. Because I guess he felt --
Mercer said that?
Yeah.
That's the way he sounded.
Yeah.
I couldn't believe it.
